Photograph: Alexander Wiaplah/AP US news US deports 20 people to Liberia, the first of 1,200 migrants under Trump deal Agreement is among largest third-country deportations driven by Trump administration’s immigration crackdown Associated Press Thu 20 Aug 2026 11.42 EDT Last modified on Thu 20 Aug 2026 11.56 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The United States sent 20 deportees to Liberia , who arrived on Thursday as part of 1,200 migrants that the African country will receive under a new deal. The deportees arrived at the Roberts international airport outside Monrovia. The Liberia-US agreement is among the largest third-country deportations driven by the Trump administration’s crackdown on immigration. The 1,200 deportees will include African nationals and also nationals from North America, South America and the Caribbean, according to the Liberian information minister, Jerolinmek Piah. During a briefing on Tuesday, Liberia’s justice minister, Natu Oswald Tweh, said that the majority of the deportees had committed migration-related violations and offenses, and that they could seek asylum in the west African country if they wished. Under a series of often-secret agreements, the Trump administration has deported thousands of people to nearly two dozen countries that are not their own, advocates say, with about 10 of them in Africa. Immigration lawyers have said the Trump administration uses deportations to third countries as a legal loophole to indirectly force asylum seekers back to their home countries. In many cases, migrants are deported to countries they have never been to or where they face safety risks and are left with little choice other than to return to the home countries they were fleeing from. https://telex.hu/after/2026/09/14/enyedi.text: Menü Kereső Enyedi Ildikó Csendes barát című filmjét nevezi Magyarország az Oscar-díjra After Pál Tamás Magyarország Enyedi Ildikó Csendes barát című filmjét nevezi az Oscar-díjra – jelentette be hétfőn a Nemzeti Filmintézet. Enyedi Ildikó legutóbbi filmjének világpremierje tavaly volt a Velencei Filmfesztiválon, ahol összesen hat díjat nyert el. Az alkotást azóta több nemzetközi fesztiválon is díjazták. A Csendes barátról szóló kritikánk itt olvasható . Az Amerikai Filmakadémia szabályzata szerint a jövő márciusban 99. alkalommal kiosztandó Oscar-díjakra a nemzetközi film kategóriában minden ország egy mozifilmet nevezhet. A magyar nevezésről döntő testület tagja volt Erdély Mátyás operatőr, Gazdag Gyula forgatókönyvíró-rendező, Gelencsér Gábor filmtörténész, kritikus, Horváth Kristóf fesztiváligazgató, Kocsis Ágnes rendező és László Sára producer. A benevezett filmek közül az Amerikai Filmakadémia tagjai választják majd ki azt az öt egész estés filmet, amelyek felkerülnek a rövidlistára, és amelyek közül kikerül az Oscar-díj nyertese. A jelöltek listáját 2027. január 21-én hozzák nyilvánosságra. Az Oscar-gálára március 14-én kerül majd sor Los Angelesben. Enyedi Ildikó korábbi alkotását, a Testről és lélekről című filmet 2018-ban jelölték Oscar-díjra. A Nemzeti Filmintézet leírása szerint a Csendes barát érzékeny és filozofikus párhuzamot von növény és ember kapcsolata között. A forgatókönyvet Enyedi írta, a látványtervező Láng Imola, a jelmeztervező Peri De Braganca, a zeneszerző Keresztes Gábor és Kelemen Kristóf, a VFX Supervisor Klingl Béla, a magyarországi casting director pedig Ascher Irma volt. A filmet a tavalyi Velencei Filmfesztiválon összesen hat díjjal – köztük a legjobb feltörekvő színésznek járó Marcello Mastroianni-díjjal Luna Wedler alakításáért – jutalmazták. A Csendes barát világszerte nagy sikerrel szerepelt a filmfesztiválokon az elmúlt hónapokban. A filmkritikusokat tömörítő nemzetközi szövetség az év öt legjobb filmje közt jelölte a Fipresci Grand Prix-re. Enyedi alkotását több országban megvásárolták helyi forgalmazók, az Egyesült Államokban a 1-2 Special forgalmazza. Februárban a 45. Magyar Filmszemlén a Csendes barát kapta meg a legjobb film díját , és alkotóit is díjazták: Pálos Gergely kapta meg a legjobb operatőr díját, Szalai Károly a legjobb vágó díját, Mécs Mónika pedig a legjobb producer díját. Photograph: EPA Yemen US officials decide against backing Saudi Arabia in Yemen after meeting Houthi leaders Armed group appears to reach agreement with Trump administration over safety of Red Sea shipping Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor Wed 16 Sep 2026 10.56 EDT Last modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 11.40 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Officials from the US met Houthi leaders over the weekend at the country’s embassy in Muscat, Oman, it has been confirmed, leading to the US decision not to intervene to help Saudi Arabia drive back a Houthi advance inside Yemen . The Houthis reassured the US that the ceasefire agreement between the two sides struck in 2025 still held and the movement had no intention of attacking US shipping in the Red Sea. Only Saudi-linked shipping was regarded as a target owing to its blockade of Yemen, the Houthis confirmed. The meeting helps to explain the decision from the US president, Donald Trump, to condemn the Houthi advance down the west coast of Yemen for threatening freedom of navigation through the Bab al-Mandab strait, but so far to reject any military response in support of Riyadh. The US is already embroiled in an expensive and resource sapping conflict with Iran , which backs the Houthis. The US labelled the Houthis as a foreign terrorist entity in March 2025, but in the recent past has met leaders from Hamas, Hezbollah and Iran. The US vice-president JD Vance confirmed on Monday that the US was in direct contact with the Houthis. The US refusal to become directly involved has put pressure on Saudi Arabia to reach either a diplomatic solution with the Houthis over the future governance of Yemen, or to try to build a regional alliance with Pakistan and Turkey to force the Houthis back. In a lightning offensive last week, the Houthis seized control of large swathes of western Yemen along the Red Sea coast. The former deputy US ambassador to Yemen, Nabeel Khoury, said a “kind of tacit understanding between the Trump administration and the Houthis” had been struck. Khoury added: “The Houthis are promising the American administration that American and international navigation will not be affected in the Red Sea, but the only danger is to Saudi ships or those carrying Saudi oil.” In a bid to build popular support against the Houthis in the region, Riyadh made the controversial claim that the Houthis had fired a drone at the holy city of Mecca on Tuesday, but the missile had been destroyed by Saudi defence forces. It said the drone was entering a prohibited airspace close to Mecca’s most holy shrines. The drone was intercepted at about 6.50pm local time on Tuesday, coalition spokesperson Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki said in a statement. Saudi Arabia said any attack on Mecca is a red line and the move was condemned in lengthy statements by the UN-recognised Yemen government based in Aden as well as the 57-country Organisation of Islamic Cooperation. The Pakistani prime minister, Shehbaz Sharif, condemned what he described as a “dastardly and heinous” attempted attack on Mecca. “The people of Pakistan are saddened and perturbed by this outrageous act,” he said in a statement posted on X. Houthi leadership – followers of a Shia Zaydism that respects the pilgrimage to Mecca – dismissed the claim as the lie of the century, adding that such worn-out lies had been used before and had fooled no one. The Houthi’s deputy foreign minister, Abdul Wahid Abu Ras, said “whoever opened the land of the two holy mosques to debauchery and entertainment parties, and whoever defiled the land of the two holy mosques by the presence of Zionist Jews in it, is the one who targets Mecca, Medina and the Islamic holy sites”. The Houthis countered that they had shot down a Saudi F-15 plane close to Marib, and attacked an Aramco plant in the Red Sea port city of Yanbu. No supporting evidence was provided by the Houthi military spokesperson, but the head of the Houthi negotiating team, Mohammed Abdul Salam, said the downing of the plane was a warning to the west not to fall victim to Saudi propaganda. Mohammed al-Farah, a Houthi political bureau member, said: “The truth is that Saudi Arabia is experiencing a real predicament in Yemen. It became embroiled in a war, a siege and an occupation, and then failed to achieve its goals. “Today, it is looking for external solutions, so it is begging the international community, warning the world about Bab al-Mandab and requesting support from Pakistan, Turkey, America, Israel and Egypt. Then it is trying to mobilise Muslims with a false pretext called ‘targeting Mecca’.” Separately, Israeli officials have leaked details of a secret meeting between military commanders from the US, Israel and several Arab states in Germany last week to discuss the war launched by Israel and the US against Iran . The report from Axios journalist Barak Ravid said the “private retreat” was organised by the commander of US Central Command (Centcom), Adm Brad Cooper. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Thing Our US morning briefing breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters after newsletter promotion Citing two unnamed Israeli officials, Ravid reported that the meeting was attended by the military chiefs of staff of Israel, Saudi Arabia the UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar Jordan and Egypt. It was the first such gathering since the US and Israel went to war with Iran more than six months ago . Israel, once a target for the Houthis, is offering to intervene in Yemen on Saudi Arabia’s behalf. Iranian security forces coordinated killing, torture and sexual abuse of protesters, says Amnesty Read more A meeting of the UN security council on Tuesday condemned any attempt to close the Red Sea, but the meeting was notable for the Russian envoy beginning to edge away from its previous stance that the UN-recognised government based in Aden was the only legitimate government inside the country. In Beijing, the Iranian foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, on Wednesday met his Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, in a bid to secure Chinese support for its plans for the future administration of the strait of Hormuz. The strait remains effectively closed owing to separate Iranian and US blockades. A Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said China does not want to see further regional tension spill over into Yemen and the Red Sea. The Chinese called on the US to return to the talks based on the memorandum of understanding agreed between the two sides in June. Beijing, the main importer of Iranian oil, is eager for a settlement and is resisting any suggestion that US secondary sanctions applied to countries trading with Iran should apply to its own country. Oil prices remain well over $100 (£74) a barrel and a key Saudi East-West pipeline remains closed because of a bombing incident. https://econotimes.com/Poland-and-Britai.text: Officials address a joint news conference at a government venue in Warsaw, Poland / EconoTimes.ai Reuters reported Tuesday that Poland and Britain signed a three-year defense plan, while Polish Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said Warsaw would work to bring Britain closer to the European Union. Signed Tuesday, the plan sets a three-year framework for military exercises and capability development. Kosiniak-Kamysz said Poland would seek to ensure Britain could benefit from SAFE, the EU’s defense financing program. Kosiniak-Kamysz made the remarks at a joint news conference with British Defense Minister Wes Streeting. Both ministers endorsed stronger European defense capacity. Kosiniak-Kamysz said that goal should not come at the expense of ties with Washington. He said Poland and Britain support strengthening the transatlantic alliance with the United States. “There is no alternative to transatlantic cooperation,” Kosiniak-Kamysz said.
